name: Neural Duplex Radiance Field
definition: A radiance field representation that uses two geometric proxy meshes (inner and outer) to define a ray segment. Instead of dense volumetric sampling, it learns to map the two endpoints of the ray segment (intersections with the inner and outer meshes) and the view direction to the final pixel color, reducing the number of sampled points per ray to two.
summary: Neural Duplex Radiance Field is a real-time view synthesis method that replaces volumetric ray marching with two proxy meshes, setting it apart by using hardware rasterization for feature interpolation instead of per-point MLP queries.
